newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian T-bills open firmer amid account buying.
newsitem.headline: Canadian T-bills open firmer amid account buying.

text.p: Canadian T-bills opened mostly firmer in quiet trade on Friday with moderate buying by accounts in the shorter end to the money market yield curve helping prices strengthen, dealers said.

"We are seeing some account buying and we don't expect it to last very long today, so that's what is creating the little bit of strength in our market," said one T-bill dealer with a bank-owned brokerage. "As we get up toward 11 o'clock it will be dead."
Canada's three-month when-issued T-bill firmed to yield 3.13 percent from 3.14 percent at Thursday's close.

Activity in the Canadian money market was light with U.S. markets closed for Independence Day. While trading is expected to taper off going into the afternoon, there has been no official call for an early close.
In other prices, the six-month when-issued T-bill firmed to yield 3.42 percent from 3.44 percent on Thursday. The one-year T-bill traded unchanged to yield 3.90 percent.
The call loan or overnight lending rate traded at 3.30 percent, near the center of the Bank of Canada's 3.0-3.5 percent target range.
